title: Frequency Tables, Dot Plots and Stem-and-Leaf Plots
seo_title: Grade 4 Dot Plots and Stem-and-Leaf Plots Worksheets (TEKS 4.9A, 4.9B, STAAR)
standard_text: 4.9A represent data on a frequency table, dot plot, or stem-and-leaf plot marked with whole numbers and fractions; 4.9B solve one- and two-step problems using data in whole number, decimal, and fraction form in a frequency table, dot plot, or stem-and-leaf plot
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 data worksheets for Texas TEKS 4.9A and 4.9B: dot plots with fractions, frequency tables, stem-and-leaf plots and one- and two-step problems. 100 STAAR-style questions with answers.
key_big: A stem is the tens digit; a leaf is the ones digit.
key_sub: Read the key first. In a dot plot each dot is one value; count the dots above each mark.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A frequency table lists each category and how many times it occurs.
  • A dot plot has one dot for each data value above a number line. Values can be whole numbers or fractions.
  • In a stem-and-leaf plot, the stem is the tens digit and each leaf is a ones digit. Read the key: 4 | 7 means 47.
  • Use the data to add, subtract and compare in one or two steps.

Examples

StemLeaf
23 7
31 5 5
42 8

Key: 2 | 3 means 23

The values are 23, 27, 31, 35, 35, 42 and 48. The greatest is 48.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading a stem as a data valueEvery value needs a stem and a leaf: 4 | 2 is 42.
Counting the leaves of the wrong stemFind the stem first, then count only its leaves.
Ignoring fractions on a dot plotRead each mark on the number line, such as 2 1/4.

faq.q: How do you read a stem-and-leaf plot?
faq.a: Put each stem with each of its leaves. With the key 3 | 6 = 36, the row 3 | 1 4 6 shows 31, 34 and 36.

faq.q: What is the difference between a dot plot and a frequency table?
faq.a: A dot plot shows each value as a dot on a number line. A frequency table lists the counts as numbers.

items.q: Aaliyah measured some seed pods. The line plot shows the lengths. How many seed pods are 1 34 inches long?
items.e: Find 1 34 on the number line. Count only the X's in that column: 2. Do not count the X's above the marks next to it.

items.q: Grace measured some ribbon pieces. The line plot shows the lengths. Which length is the most common?
items.e: The most common length has the tallest stack of X's. The stack above 1 78 has 3 X's, more than any other.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class measured some crickets. The line plot shows the lengths. How many crickets did the class measure in all?
items.e: Each X is one cricket. Add the X's in every column: 1 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 1 = 13.

items.q: Ms. Lee's class measured some crayons. The line plot shows the lengths. How many crayons are 3 28 inches long?
items.e: The marks are labeled in simplest form. 3 28 = 3 14, so look at the mark labeled 3 14. Count the X's above it: 3.

items.q: Jayden measured some shells. The line plot shows the lengths. How long is the longest shell?
items.e: Look for the X that is farthest to the right: it is above 2 58. The mark 2 34 has no X, so no shell is that long.

items.q: Mr. Diaz's class measured some caterpillars. The line plot shows the lengths. How many caterpillars are 1 inch long?

items.q: Ms. Lee's class measured some snail shells. The line plot shows the lengths. How many snail shells are longer than 78 inch?
items.e: Longer means to the right of 78. Do not count the X's above 78 itself. Add the X's to the right: 2 + 1 = 3.

sets.title: Add and compare data on dot plots

items.q: Zoe measured some pine cones. The line plot shows the lengths. The pine cones that are 2 58 inches long are put end to end. What is their total length?
items.e: There are 3 X's above 2 58, so add 2 58 3 times. Add the fractions: 58 + 58 + 58 = 158. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. 158 = 1 78, so 6 + 1 78 = 7 78 inches.

items.q: Camila measured some crickets. The line plot shows the lengths. The crickets that are 1 14 inches long are put end to end. What is their total length?
items.e: There are 2 X's above 1 14, so add 1 14 2 times. Add the fractions: 14 + 14 = 24. Add the whole numbers: 1 + 1 = 2. Put them together: 2 24 inches.

items.q: Diego measured some snail shells. The line plot shows the lengths. The snail shells that are 1 34 inches long are put end to end. What is their total length?
items.e: There are 4 X's above 1 34, so add 1 34 4 times. Add the fractions: 34 + 34 + 34 + 34 = 124. Add the whole numbers: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4. 124 = 3, so 4 + 3 = 7 inches.

items.q: Isaac measured some caterpillars. The line plot shows the lengths. The caterpillars that are 1 58 inches long are put end to end. What is their total length?
items.e: There are 2 X's above 1 58, so add 1 58 2 times. Add the fractions: 58 + 58 = 108. Add the whole numbers: 1 + 1 = 2. 108 = 1 28, so 2 + 1 28 = 3 28 inches.

items.q: Ava measured some leaves. The line plot shows the lengths. The leaves that are 1 12 inches long are put end to end. What is their total length?
items.e: There are 3 X's above 1 12, so add 1 12 3 times. Add the fractions: 12 + 12 + 12 = 32. Add the whole numbers: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. 32 = 1 12, so 3 + 1 12 = 4 12 inches.

items.q: Ms. Lee's class measured some ribbon pieces. The line plot shows the lengths. The ribbon pieces that are 1 38 inches long are put end to end. What is their total length?
items.e: There are 2 X's above 1 38, so add 1 38 2 times. Add the fractions: 38 + 38 = 68. Add the whole numbers: 1 + 1 = 2. Put them together: 2 68 inches.

items.q: Emma measured some beetles. The line plot shows the lengths. The beetles that are 1 12 inches long are put end to end. What is their total length?
items.e: There are 3 X's above 1 12, so add 1 12 3 times. Add the fractions: 12 + 12 + 12 = 32. Add the whole numbers: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. 32 = 1 12, so 3 + 1 12 = 4 12 inches.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class measured some seed pods. The line plot shows the lengths. The seed pods that are 2 18 inches long are put end to end. What is their total length?
items.e: There are 3 X's above 2 18, so add 2 18 3 times. Add the fractions: 18 + 18 + 18 = 38. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. Put them together: 6 38 inches.

items.q: Ms. Lee's class measured some earthworms. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of all the earthworms that are 4 38 inches or 4 34 inches long?
items.e: The plot has 3 X's above 4 38 and 2 X's above 4 34. Write them in eighths: 4 34 = 4 68. Add the fractions: 38 + 38 + 38 + 68 + 68 = 218. Add the whole numbers: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 20. 218 = 2 58, so 20 + 2 58 = 22 58 inches.

items.q: Jayden measured some feathers. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of all the feathers that are 2 38 inches or 2 12 inches long?
items.e: The plot has 3 X's above 2 38 and 2 X's above 2 12. Write them in eighths: 2 12 = 2 48. Add the fractions: 38 + 38 + 38 + 48 + 48 = 178. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10. 178 = 2 18, so 10 + 2 18 = 12 18 inches.

items.q: Camila measured some caterpillars. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest caterpillar than the shortest caterpillar?
items.e: Longest: 2 38 inches. Shortest: 1 34 inches. Write them in eighths: 1 34 = 1 68. Subtract: 2 38 − 1 68. 38 is less than 68, so rename 1 whole as 88: 2 38 = 1 118. Subtract the fractions: 118 − 68 = 58. Subtract the whole numbers: 1 − 1 = 0. The answer is 58 inch.

items.q: Luis measured some crickets. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest cricket than the shortest cricket?
items.e: Longest: 1 12 inches. Shortest: 78 inch. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line. Write them in eighths: 1 12 = 1 48. Subtract: 1 48 − 78. 48 is less than 78, so rename 1 whole as 88: 1 48 = 128. Subtract the fractions: 128 − 78 = 58. The answer is 58 inch.

items.q: Nevaeh measured some pine cones. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest pine cone than the shortest pine cone?
items.e: Longest: 3 12 inches. Shortest: 2 inches. Write them in fourths: 3 12 = 3 24. Subtract: 3 24 − 2. Subtract the whole numbers: 3 − 2 = 1. The answer is 1 24 inches.

items.q: Aaliyah measured some ribbon pieces. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest ribbon piece than the shortest ribbon piece?
items.e: Longest: 3 78 inches. Shortest: 3 18 inches. Subtract: 3 78 − 3 18. Subtract the fractions: 78 − 18 = 68. Subtract the whole numbers: 3 − 3 = 0. The answer is 68 inch.

items.q: Marcus measured some feathers. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest feather than the shortest feather?
items.e: Longest: 3 18 inches. Shortest: 2 38 inches. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line. Subtract: 3 18 − 2 38. 18 is less than 38, so rename 1 whole as 88: 3 18 = 2 98. Subtract the fractions: 98 − 38 = 68. Subtract the whole numbers: 2 − 2 = 0. The answer is 68 inch.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class measured some beetles. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest beetle than the shortest beetle?
items.e: Longest: 2 12 inches. Shortest: 1 14 inches. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line. Write them in fourths: 2 12 = 2 24. Subtract: 2 24 − 1 14. Subtract the fractions: 24 − 14 = 14. Subtract the whole numbers: 2 − 1 = 1. The answer is 1 14 inches.

items.q: Elijah measured some earthworms. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest earthworm than the shortest earthworm?
items.e: Longest: 2 58 inches. Shortest: 2 inches. Subtract: 2 58 − 2. Subtract the whole numbers: 2 − 2 = 0. The answer is 58 inch.

items.q: Noah measured some crayons. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest crayon than the shortest crayon?
items.e: Longest: 3 58 inches. Shortest: 2 78 inches. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line. Subtract: 3 58 − 2 78. 58 is less than 78, so rename 1 whole as 88: 3 58 = 2 138. Subtract the fractions: 138 − 78 = 68. Subtract the whole numbers: 2 − 2 = 0. The answer is 68 inch.

items.q: Mrs. Green's class measured some leaves. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest leaf than the shortest leaf?
items.e: Longest: 3 inches. Shortest: 1 12 inches. Write them in fourths: 1 12 = 1 24. Subtract: 3 − 1 24. There is no fraction to take 24 from, so rename 1 whole: 3 = 2 44. Subtract the fractions: 44 − 24 = 24. Subtract the whole numbers: 2 − 1 = 1. The answer is 1 24 inches.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class measured some acorns. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest acorn than the shortest acorn?
items.e: Longest: 1 58 inches. Shortest: 34 inch. Write them in eighths: 34 = 68. Subtract: 1 58 − 68. 58 is less than 68, so rename 1 whole as 88: 1 58 = 138. Subtract the fractions: 138 − 68 = 78. The answer is 78 inch.
